answer: Bonded reputation resists fake identities: each agent must lock a refundable stake and earn a verifiable history of completed work before trading at full limits. A newcomer is like a lone island, trusted only with small tasks until attested deliveries accumulate. Splitting one identity into many does not multiply trust, since the stake is divided and every copy must separately earn history. A zephyr of cheap fakes carries little weight, while a gale of coordinated fakes must fund and age each identity, making a large attack costlier than what it could steal.
